questions.question: An affine subspace of $V$ is a set $\{\boldsymbol{v}\}+W=\{\boldsymbol{v}+\boldsymbol{w}\colon\boldsymbol{w}\in W\}$ with $W$ a subspace of $V$ and $\boldsymbol{v}\in V$. Which subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is an affine subspace?

An affine subspace of $V$ is a set $\{\boldsymbol{v}\}+W=\{\boldsymbol{v}+\boldsymbol{w}\colon\boldsymbol{w}\in W\}$ with $W$ a subspace of $V$ and $\boldsymbol{v}\in V$. Which condition is necessary and sufficient for $\{\boldsymbol{v}\}+W$ to be a linear subspace of $V$?

A nonempty $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ is affine iff $\lambda\boldsymbol{x}+(1-\lambda)\boldsymbol{y}\in S$ for all $\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y}\in S$ and all $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$. Is the segment $\{\lambda\boldsymbol{x}+(1-\lambda)\boldsymbol{y}\colon\lambda\in[0,1]\}$ with $\boldsymbol{x}\neq\boldsymbol{y}$ affine?
options: Yes; it contains every combination with $\lambda\in[0,1]$
No; it is convex, but $\lambda=2$ gives a point outside
Yes; it is the line through $\boldsymbol{x}$ and $\boldsymbol{y}$
No; it does not contain the origin $\boldsymbol{0}$

questions.question: $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ is an affine subspace, so $S=\{\boldsymbol{v}\}+W$ for some subspace $W$ and vector $\boldsymbol{v}$. How can the direction space $W$ be recovered from $S$ alone?
options: As the set $S$ itself, since $S$ and $W$ have the same points
As the span of all points of $S$, so as to include $\boldsymbol{0}$
As all differences $\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{y}$ of two points of $S$

questions.question: An affine subspace of $V$ is a set $\{\boldsymbol{v}\}+W=\{\boldsymbol{v}+\boldsymbol{w}\colon\boldsymbol{w}\in W\}$ with $W$ a subspace of $V$ and $\boldsymbol{v}\in V$. The dimension of $\{\boldsymbol{v}\}+W$ is $\dim W$. What is the dimension of the line $L=\{(x,y)\colon x+y=1\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$?
options: $1$, the dimension of its direction space
$2$, because points of $L$ have two coordinates

questions.question: The system $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ with a $3\times5$ matrix $A$ of rank $2$ is consistent. What is the dimension of its solution set, an affine subspace of $\mathbb{R}^5$?
Let $S=\{(0,0,2)^{\top}\}+\operatorname{span}\{(1,0,-1)^{\top},(0,1,-1)^{\top}\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Which point lies in $S$?
Which equation describes the line in $\mathbb{R}^2$ through $(1,2)$ and $(3,3)$, the affine subspace $\{(1,2)^{\top}\}+\operatorname{span}\{(2,1)^{\top}\}$?
Let $L=\{(1,2)^{\top}\}+\operatorname{span}\{(2,1)^{\top}\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$. Which description gives the same set $L$?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}=(3,6)^{\top}$, the vector $\boldsymbol{x}_p=(3,0)^{\top}$ solves $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$. What is the full solution set?
Let $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ be consistent with $\boldsymbol{b}\neq\boldsymbol{0}$, and let $S$ be its solution set. Which description of $S$ is correct?
options: $S$ is affine but not a subspace, since $\boldsymbol{0}\notin S$
$S$ is a subspace, since it is closed under addition
$S$ is affine only if $A$ is square and invertible
$S$ is not affine, since differences of solutions are not solutions

questions.question: In $\mathbb{R}^2$ let $L_1=\{(x,y)\colon y=x+1\}$ and $L_2=\{(x,y)\colon y=-x+1\}$, two affine lines. Which of these sets is an affine subspace?
options: $L_1\cup L_2$, a union of two affine lines
$L_1\cup\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$, the line with the origin added

questions.question: Hyperplanes in $\mathbb{R}^n$ are written $\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=c\}$ with $\boldsymbol{a}\neq\boldsymbol{0}$, the affine subspaces of dimension $n-1$. Why is $\boldsymbol{a}\neq\boldsymbol{0}$ required?
options: For $\boldsymbol{a}=\boldsymbol{0}$ the set is the origin only
For $\boldsymbol{a}=\boldsymbol{0}$ the set is a line instead
For $\boldsymbol{a}=\boldsymbol{0}$ the set is empty or all of $\mathbb{R}^n$

questions.question: Let $S=\{(x,y)\colon xy=0\}$, the union of the two coordinate axes in $\mathbb{R}^2$. Which affine combination $\lambda\boldsymbol{x}+(1-\lambda)\boldsymbol{y}$ with $\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y}\in S$ shows that $S$ is not affine?
Let $L=\{(1,0)^{\top}\}+\operatorname{span}\{(1,1)^{\top}\}$ and $M=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. The image $\{M\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{x}\in L\}$ is affine. Which description is it?
An affine subspace $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ contains $\boldsymbol{p}=(1,1,1)^{\top}$ and $\boldsymbol{q}=(2,3,0)^{\top}$. Which point must also lie in $S$?

For an $m\times n$ matrix $A$, the solution set of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ is affine whenever it is nonempty; affine subspaces are nonempty by convention. For which $A$ is it an affine subspace for every $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$?
options: For every $A$, since $\{\boldsymbol{x}_p\}+\operatorname{Null}(A)$ is always affine
Exactly when $\operatorname{rank}A=m$, so that every $\boldsymbol{b}$ is attained
Exactly when $m=n$ and $A$ is invertible, so $\boldsymbol{x}$ is unique

questions.question: Let $S_1=\{\boldsymbol{v}\}+W$ and $S_2=\{\boldsymbol{v}'\}+W$ be affine subspaces of $V$ with the same direction space $W$. Which statement about $S_1$ and $S_2$ is correct?
options: They always meet in exactly one point
They are either equal or disjoint
They can share a part and still differ

questions.question: Describe the intersection of the planes $x+y+z=1$ and $x-y=0$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ as an affine subspace $\{\boldsymbol{v}\}+W$.
What is the dimension of the solution set of $x_1-x_2+2x_3=3$, $2x_1-2x_2+4x_3=6$, $x_1+x_3=1$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$?
options: None: dependent rows mean no solution
